recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to light gray (#F2F2F2) and draw a thin dark-red (#8B0000) rectangular border around the entire slide edge. 2. Add centered title text box near top: 'Some Monotonically increase  Functions' (note double space), bold, dark red (#8B0000), large sans-serif (~32pt). 3. Add a yellow (#FFFACD) circle with black outline at top-right containing '23' in black. 4. Create three equal-size graph panels in a horizontal row in the upper-middle area. 5. Left panel: draw a light grid with x/y axes, plot a straight line through the origin with slope 1/2 (purple-gray, arrowheads both ends), add red text 'y = 1/2 x' at upper right of the line, add a green up arrow and green right arrow, plus a small pen icon near the label. 6. Center panel: draw grid with y-axis ticks -6 to 6 and x-axis ticks 1 to 11, axis labels 'x' and 'y'; plot a red log₂(x) curve rising steeply from lower left and flattening; label 'y = log₂(x)' in red; add green up and right arrows. 7. Right panel: draw grid with x ticks 2-14 and y ticks -4 to 6; plot a gray ln(x) curve; label 'f(x) = ln(x)' in red; add green up and right arrows. 8. Leave the bottom ~35% of the slide empty.
